newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank not to tighten liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank not to tighten liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank has no immediate plan to tighten its stable-to-loose monetary policy, saying the recent stock rally showed investors' confidence in an economic recovery, a senior bank official said on Thursday.
"The central bank thinks the stock market's bull run shows investors are confident in the domestic economic recovery," bank official Lee Sheng-yen told reporters.
"There is no need for the central bank to show special concerns about the market's sharp gains at the moment," Lee said, implying the bank would not tighten its money policy.

On Thursday, the weighted index ended 112.18 points or 1.51 percent higher at a new six-year high of 7,536.28. That surpassed the 7,424.10 close on Wednesday, and was the market's highest finish since it ended at 7,857.01 on June 2, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$123.16 billion.
Thursday's gains, marking the market's eighth consecutive high close, triggered concerns that the central bank may move to tighten liquidity to smooth the over-heated market.
Lee said recent stock rally did not affect other financial markets.
Taiwan's index, backed by widespread hope that the island's economy was heading into a recovery, has already gained more than 700 points in 1997.
